about: Converter cases. Each expected file is what the reference normalizer (the implementation the format comes from, as fixed on 2026-11-14) wrote for the same input; convert.py must write the same bytes. Synthetic text only.

fields.language_recognized_by_reference: the input names no language; the reference implementation recognized this one on the device. convert.py writes "unknown" unless told, so the test supplies this value (SPEC.md, Known gaps, G-11)
fields.unreadable: the reason the converter must give instead of a file
fields.truncated: the input is treated as cut off at a size limit

Podcasting 2.0 JSON whose times are not times: "nan", "inf", 1e300, negative numbers, 100 hours and more, "1e308:00". Each such row keeps its text and gets [--:--:--]; 359999 is the last time that can be written.
Lines that start with a time, one written "0:31:". The title line before the first time stays a segment of its own and the timed lines keep their times.
"Note:" is not a speaker; "Dr. Aalto:" is. An unlabelled line after a blank line has no stated speaker.
"Speaker 1 (00:02):" lines give the speaker and the time.
"Name 0:12" lines.
Captions that repeat the line before, ">>" marks, font tags, a sentence said twice.
Rolling captions with karaoke times: every line arrives two or three times.
A bare list of rows with name, start and text; a clock string as a time; an empty name.
Markdown with times inside the lines, a title, an address line, a rule, a sponsor read and a phrase said twice.
Two <v> voices in one cue, a cue name, a sound note, a sponsor read, hours. Escaped text (<once>) stays as <once>; a cue an hour later starts a new segment.
One "transcript" string, read as plain text; language from "lang".
